channel.title: JustinCredible Science
channel.description: Discoveries, research and the natural world, explained without the jargon.

item.title: Mountains Grew Taller in Two Big Spurts, and a New Study Links Them to the Rise of Oxygen and Complex Life
item.description: A study in Science Advances, announced November 13, 2026, by researchers from the University of British Columbia, Utrecht University and others, finds mountain belts got much taller in two jumps, around 2.3 billion and 800 million years ago, roughly when Earth's oxygen rose.

item.title: Webb and Gemini Find the Earliest Known Close Pair of Quasars, and It Puzzles Astronomers
item.description: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope and Gemini North report a compact pair of quasars seen just 900 million years after the Big Bang, powered by black holes of 1.5 billion and 400 million solar masses. The study appeared in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.
